findings.summary: latest-task API filters for IN_PROGRESS/NEEDS_HELP/NEEDS_REVIEW but tasks are never transitioned from PENDING to IN_PROGRESS, so the API always returns null and DB-based session restoration never works
findings.failure_scenario: User creates a task (status defaults to PENDING per start-task/route.ts line 24) then opens the app from a different browser with no local storage. loadTaskFromLocalStorage returns null, so fetchLatestTask is called. The API queries for tasks with status IN (IN_PROGRESS, NEEDS_HELP, NEEDS_REVIEW) but finds none because the task is still PENDING. Returns {task: null}. The user sees an empty chat and cannot resume the existing task — they must start a brand new task.

findings.summary: completeTask() marks the task COMPLETED and then the loop breaks, but isOnAutopilot is never reset to false, deadlocking all subsequent triggerAgentWithMessage calls because setAutopilot(true) returns early when isOnAutopilot is already true
findings.failure_scenario: First task runs to natural completion (AI responds without tool use). completeTask() at line 474 sets DB status to COMPLETED, then line 475 breaks the while loop. isOnAutopilot remains true. A second task job arrives at the worker: triggerAgentWithMessage adds the new message to messageStore and calls setAutopilot(true), which checks isOnAutopilot === value (lines 60-62) — both are true — so it returns immediately without calling runAgent(). The second task stays PENDING forever, its message never processed.

findings.summary: Initial session message from fetchLatestTask uses raw Prisma JSON content without transforming through the same format as /api/messages, so images in tool_result blocks fail to render due to source vs image shape mismatch
findings.failure_scenario: A task with image-bearing messages is loaded via fetchLatestTask. The raw DB content for an image block is {type:'image', source:{data:'...', media_type:'image/png', type:'base64'}} (per the Prisma schema comment at schema.prisma line 70). The MessageItem component at MessageItem.tsx line 36 checks block.type === 'image' && block.image — but raw DB content has 'source' not 'image', so block.image is undefined. The image does not render, showing a blank message instead.

findings.summary: loadSession sets the initial message via setMessages but fails to call setLastMessageId(initialMessage.id), leaving lastMessageId as null and bypassing the incremental-fetch optimization on every subsequent poll
findings.failure_scenario: Initial session loads with one message (id='abc-123'). lastMessageId stays null. Every 2-second poll sends lastMessageId=null to /api/messages, so the server returns ALL messages from the task. The client deduplicates via processedMessageIds, but the server-side createdAt > lastMessage.createdAt optimization at messages/route.ts lines 80-87 is never exercised. Every poll wastes DB bandwidth re-fetching and re-transmitting already-seen messages.

findings.summary: startNewConversation is exported from the useChatSession hook but never destructured or called in page.tsx; the corresponding 'New Conversation' button is commented out in Header.tsx — dead code and incomplete feature
findings.failure_scenario: Maintenance cost only. The hook return at line 249 includes startNewConversation but page.tsx lines 11-18 destructure only messages, input, setInput, isLoading, isLoadingSession, handleSend. Header.tsx lines 7-9 and 20-28 have commented-out props and button markup for a 'New Conversation' feature. The function exists but is unreachable, and the UI to trigger it was never un-commented — a partially implemented feature left in dead code.
